title: Ind-constructible sheaves are closed under filtered colimits and sums
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and a separated scheme $X$ of finite type over $k$, in the standing geometric setting of the source. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and a finite intermediate extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $\Lambda=\underline E$ or $\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}$ be the condensed coefficient ring of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Work in $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X}(\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\operatorname{Ab}))$, the internal-module category of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], with $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$. Let $\operatorname{Cons}(X,\Lambda)$ use the finite constant local-model convention of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and let $\operatorname{IndCons}(X,\Lambda)$ consist of the objects isomorphic to small filtered colimits in $\mathcal M$ of constructible objects. Here small means small in the chosen universe of the site and coefficient sheaves.

If $(B_\lambda)_{\lambda\in I}$ is a small filtered diagram in $\operatorname{IndCons}(X,\Lambda)$, then its colimit $B$ in $\mathcal M$ belongs to $\operatorname{IndCons}(X,\Lambda)$. For every small set $S$, the direct sum in $\mathcal M$ of a family $(B_s)_{s\in S}$ in $\operatorname{IndCons}(X,\Lambda)$ belongs to $\operatorname{IndCons}(X,\Lambda)$, including $S=\varnothing$.

proof.text: Recall the unit's definition: $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$ consists of the small filtered colimits, in $\Mod(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$, of objects of $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$. Let $\mathcal K$ be the category of pairs $(\lambda,c\colon C\to B_\lambda)$ with $C$ constructible; a morphism $(\lambda,c)\to(\mu,c')$ is a pair $(u,f)$ with $u\colon\lambda\to\mu$ in $I$ and $f\colon C\to C'$ satisfying $c'f=B(u)c$. Identities and composition are componentwise, and $(\lambda,c)\mapsto C$, $(u,f)\mapsto f$ defines a diagram. By [det-ind-heart-canonical-presentation], each $J(B_\lambda)$ is essentially small. Since $I$ is small, the union over $\lambda$ of sets of representatives of these objects is a set of representatives for $\mathcal K$; its morphisms are sets of pairs $(u,f)$. Thus $\mathcal K$ is essentially small, and a small skeleton may be used for its colimit.

*$\mathcal K$ is filtered.* Every $J(B_\lambda)$ is nonempty and filtered by [det-ind-heart-canonical-presentation]. Choose $\lambda\in I$ and an object of $J(B_\lambda)$ to obtain an object of $\mathcal K$. For $(\lambda,c\colon C	o B_\lambda)$ and $(
u,d\colon D	o B_
u)$, choose $u\colon\lambda	o\mu$ and $v\colon
u	o\mu$ in $I$. A common successor of $(C,B(u)c)$ and $(D,B(v)d)$ in $J(B_\mu)$ gives a common successor in $\mathcal K$. For parallel arrows $(u,f),(v,g)\colon(\lambda,c)ightrightarrows(\mu,d)$, choose $w\colon\mu	oho$ with $wu=wv$. The maps $f,g$ are now parallel morphisms from $(C,B(wu)c)$ to $(D,B(w)d)$ in $J(B_ho)$. Choose $h\colon(D,B(w)d)	o(A,a)$ there with $hf=hg$. Then $(w,h)\colon(\mu,d)	o(ho,a)$ equalizes the original two arrows, since its composites have components $(wu,hf)=(wv,hg)$. These are the three filteredness conditions.

*Colimit.* For any $\Lambda_X$-module sheaf $M$, restrict a cocone on $\mathcal K$ to each fibre $J(B_\lambda)$. The canonical presentation in [det-ind-heart-canonical-presentation] gives unique maps $h_\lambda\colon B_\lambda\to M$. For $u\colon\lambda\to\mu$, the arrow $(u,\mathrm{id}_C)\colon(\lambda,c)\to(\mu,B(u)c)$ implies $h_\lambda c=h_\mu B(u)c$ for every $c$; the colimit property of $J(B_\lambda)$ gives $h_\lambda=h_\mu B(u)$. Conversely, such a compatible family gives the cocone $h_\lambda c$, because for $(u,f)$ one has $h_\mu c'f=h_\mu B(u)c=h_\lambda c$. The two constructions are inverse. Thus cocones on $\mathcal K$ are exactly cocones from $(B_\lambda)$ to $M$, naturally in $M$, so $B$ with its maps $C\to B_\lambda\to B$ is the colimit over $\mathcal K$. Steps 1 and 2 show that this is a small filtered colimit of constructible sheaves, proving the first assertion.

*Direct sums.* For a finite subset $T\subset S$, choose presentations $B_s=\varinjlim_{\alpha_s\in A_s}C^{(s)}_{\alpha_s}$ from the definition of $\IndCons$. The finite product $A=\prod_{s\in T}A_s$ is filtered: it is nonempty, and common successors and equalizers of parallel arrows are chosen coordinatewise. The zero sheaf is constructible, and finite sums of constructibles are constructible by [sk-lem-coefficient-heart]: use $0\to C\to C\oplus D\to D\to0$ and closure under extensions. A cocone from $\bigoplus_{s\in T}C^{(s)}_{\alpha_s}$ to $M$ is exactly a compatible family of maps $C^{(s)}_{\alpha_s}\to M$ for each $s$. Indeed, restrict to each summand; its map is independent of the other coordinates because any two choices of those coordinates have a common successor. The presentation of $B_s$ then gives a unique map $B_s\to M$, and the coproduct property gives a unique map $\bigoplus_{s\in T}B_s\to M$. Conversely these maps define the cocone by composition. Hence the colimit over $A$ is $\bigoplus_{s\in T}B_s$, so finite sums lie in $\IndCons$. For $T=\varnothing$, the product category is the one-object category and its diagram is the zero constructible sheaf. Finally the poset of finite subsets of $S$ is nonempty and directed by union. A compatible family of maps from the finite subsums to $M$ is uniquely determined by its singleton maps $B_s\to M$, and conversely those maps extend to every finite subsum. Its colimit is therefore $\bigoplus_{s\in S}B_s$. The first assertion applied to this filtered diagram proves the result, also for $S=\varnothing$.

Step 2: nonempty, common successors via a common index mu, and parallel arrows equalized by (w,h), where I verified that the morphism equations hold. This uses the filteredness of J(B_rho). Step 4: finite sums of constructible sheaves are constructible as extensions, by sk-lem-coefficient-heart (1). The product of filtered categories is filtered coordinatewise. Independence of the other coordinates holds via a common successor that is the identity on coordinate s. The finite-subset colimit then gives the arbitrary sum. The edge cases T=∅ and S=∅ are handled. Route: both proof_deps are inside the unit's route. There is no cycle and no tool_uses.
